+# Acceptance Criteria
+
+Rules:
+
+- Criteria lines use the exact format `- ACn: <criterion>`.
+- Every criterion ends with [verify: exec `<command>`],
+  [verify: invariant `<command>`], [verify: judged] or
+  [verify: none — <reason>].
+- After `flow freeze` this file is checksum-protected: any edit outside
+  `keryx flow ac update` fails every gate and status transition.
+- Completion requires every ACn to be confirmed via
+  `keryx flow ac confirm <id> <ACn>`.
+
+Commands run from the repository (worktree) root. "The browser dev build" is
+`cd apps/desktop && bun run dev:browser` opened on this repository with a built graph.
+
+## Criteria
+
+- AC1: `layoutNeighborhood` places every first-step neighbour whose only edges with the root point at the root left of the root, every neighbour the root points at right of it, and no two laid-out boxes (nodes, group captions, overflow entries) overlap, for a 31-node depth-1 projection of mixed `contains` and `imports` edges. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/graphLayout.test.ts`]
+- AC2: When a side has more neighbours than the column cap of 12, the layout shows exactly 12 nodes in that column plus one overflow entry whose hidden count equals that side's neighbour count minus 12; a 200-node, 269-edge depth-2 projection lays out with no overlapping boxes and at most 12 nodes per column. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/graphLayout.test.ts`]
+- AC3: Every second-step node is placed in the outer column on the side of the first-step node it is attached to, further from the root than every first-step node on that side. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/graphLayout.test.ts`]
+- AC4: `RelationshipGraph` renders an HTML caption with the root title and the incoming and outgoing counts (and the word "limited" for a truncated projection) and an HTML legend that names, with human-readable labels, exactly the node kinds and line styles present in the projection; the style mapping is a pure exported function that gives each of the seven node kinds a distinct shape-or-border treatment and maps the nine relationship kinds onto solid, dashed and dotted lines. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/RelationshipGraph.dom.test.tsx`]
+- AC5: In the browser dev build at a 1180×780 window with the details panel open, graph node labels render at 9 px or more and no two nodes overlap, both for a module with at least 30 neighbours at depth 1 and for a 200-node projection at depth 2 (measured on the live cytoscape instance: label font size × zoom, and node bounding boxes). [verify: judged]
+- AC6: Changing `data-theme` or `data-palette` on the document element re-colours the mounted graph without a selection change: after the switch the label colour equals the new theme's `--fg`. [verify: judged]
+- AC7: `NodeDetailsPanel` shows the selected node's kind as a text badge, its title, its repository path with a "Copy path" control that writes the path to the clipboard, and "N incoming · M outgoing" counts computed from the root-adjacent edges of the `relationships` projection, with "limited" when it is truncated. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/NodeDetailsPanel.dom.test.tsx`]
+- AC8: Relationships is the default tab and lists root-adjacent relationships grouped by direction and then relationship kind; activating a row calls `onSelect` with that neighbour's id; relationships between two non-root nodes are listed in a separate group whose rows can open either endpoint; a change of `revealRelationships` switches to the Relationships tab. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/NodeDetailsPanel.dom.test.tsx src/metaproject/RelationshipList.dom.test.tsx`]
+- AC9: A linked-document preview contains no Markdown markers and skips metadata: for a page whose body starts with a `> **Covers:**` blockquote line followed by a prose paragraph, the preview is that prose paragraph with no `>`, `**`, emphasis underscores or backticks. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/NodeDetailsPanel.dom.test.tsx`]
+- AC10: Explorer state survives leaving the work view: in the browser dev build, after selecting a node in Graph with a non-empty query and the panel open, switching to Flows and back shows the same view, query, selection, filters, open panel and an available Back button. [verify: judged]
+- AC11: Back steps through in-view navigation: after selecting nodes A, then B, then C in Graph, Back shows B and Back again shows A; typing in the search field adds no history entries. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx`]
+- AC12: "Find a Wiki page" for a node with no matching page shows, in the article area, an empty state that names the searched text, and renders no wiki article. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx`]
+- AC13: The Wiki view's relationships read does not depend on Graph filter state: with Graph depth set to 2 and a relationship type unticked, the neighbours request issued in Wiki mode has depth 1, direction "both" and every non-symbol relationship kind. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx`]
+- AC14: A rebuild never leaves its control stuck: when the catalog is reloaded while a rebuild is in flight, then after the rebuild resolves successfully the "Rebuild graph" control is enabled again and the catalog is read again. · sensitive: failure-scenario [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx`]
+- AC15: A failed protocol negotiation is recoverable: the error is shown with a Retry control and without "Loading project knowledge…"; activating Retry negotiates again and, on success, loads the catalog. · sensitive: failure-scenario [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx`]
+- AC16: A wiki link whose target is not among the loaded nodes is resolved with one lookup read and opens the target; when no node has that path, a visible message names the unresolved path; a percent-encoded href and an href with a leading "/" resolve to the right repository path. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx`]
+- AC17: In Graph mode the relationship list is rendered in the details panel and not under the canvas; filter controls carry human-readable labels; `defines` and `calls` are disabled with a stated reason when the catalog reports no symbol layer; the list header shows "shown of total" from `catalog.counts` instead of the "Catalog is limited" banner; the selected list row is scrolled into view when the selection changes; while relationships for a new selection load, the previous graph stays rendered and is marked busy. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bun test src/metaproject/MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx`]
+- AC18: The replaced panel file is gone: `apps/desktop/src/metaproject/GraphNodePanel.tsx` does not exist. [verify: invariant `test ! -e apps/desktop/src/metaproject/GraphNodePanel.tsx`]
+- AC19: The desktop app type-checks and its whole test suite passes. [verify: exec `cd apps/desktop && bunx tsc --noEmit && bun test src`]
+- AC20: In the browser dev build, in a dark and a light theme, at 1180×780 and 1440×900: the graph shows incoming neighbours left and outgoing neighbours right of the selected node with group captions and a legend; the details panel shows a header, facts, a tab bar with counts and one primary action per tab; no text overlaps or is clipped. At 720×480 with the panel closed and no warning banner, at least 140 px of graph height is visible without scrolling, and the open panel leaves part of the content visible. [verify: judged]
+- AC21: `docs/docs/guides/desktop-metaproject.md` describes the column layout, the legend, the "+N more" entry, the panel's Relationships / Wiki / OpenSpec tabs and that Back steps through selections; it no longer says the Wiki view shows "the same search and selection as Graph"; its relationship-type table still lists every type. [verify: judged]

+# Desktop Metaproject: readable neighbourhood graph, node summary panel and explorer navigation fixes
+
+Status: formalized
+Source: user description (owner's review request of 2026-11-23, then "start with the graph and the details panel")
+
+## Problem
+
+The Metaproject screen of Keryx Desktop (`apps/desktop/src/metaproject/`) does not let a
+developer read what a project object is connected to. A review of the shipped screen on this
+repository (4,659 files, 200 modules, 125 wiki pages) measured, in the browser dev build:
+
+- **The graph is unreadable.** At the default 1180×780 window the canvas gets 440×194 px (9% of
+  the window). Every neighbour sits on one ring regardless of direction and depth, as an identical
+  grey circle; labels render at 3.3–5.5 px; edge kinds are passed to cytoscape but never drawn;
+  there is no legend. At depth 2 the ring is 200 nodes spaced 2.6 px apart with a 13.6 px diameter.
+- **The node details panel says nothing about the node.** It is 380 px wide and holds only a
+  Wiki / OpenSpec document lookup. Its text uses three sizes (12/13/15 px) and two colours; section
+  heading and body are the same size; every button looks the same; the previews show raw Markdown
+  (`> **Covers:** …`).
+- **Navigation and state are fragile.** Leaving the work view destroys mode, query, selection and
+  Back history. Back ignores hops between graph nodes. "Find a Wiki page" lands on "No results"
+  next to an unrelated article. Graph filters silently change the Relationships block in Wiki
+  (13 → 350 relationships). "Rebuilding…" can stick. A failed protocol negotiation leaves
+  "Loading project knowledge…" forever. Wiki links to pages outside the loaded 200 nodes do
+  nothing.
+
+The owner's stated complaints: the graph is not understandable, and in the node details
+everything visually merges. (The third complaint, a tree instead of the flat sidebar list, needs a
+new backend action and is a separate piece of work.)
+
+## Expected Outcome
+
+- The graph is a readable local neighbourhood: incoming neighbours left of the selected node,
+  outgoing right, second-step nodes further out; node kind and relationship kind are visible on the
+  canvas and explained by a legend; labels are legible at the default window size; an over-full side
+  is capped with a "+N more" entry instead of overlapping.
+- The node details panel is a summary of the node: identity, path with copy, relationship counts,
+  the relationships themselves grouped by direction and kind, then linked documents — with a visible
+  hierarchy built from the app's existing tokens and patterns.
+- Explorer state survives leaving the work view; Back steps through in-view navigation; the Find,
+  Rebuild, negotiation and wiki-link dead ends are gone; Wiki relationships no longer depend on Graph
+  filter state.
+
+## Outcome criteria
+
+- On the default 1180×780 window, a module with 30 or more neighbours is readable in the graph
+  without zooming: rendered label size is at least 9 px (it was 3.3–5.5 px), measured in the browser
+  dev build before and after.
+
+## Out of Scope
+
+- The sidebar tree (needs a new explorer action and a relaxed capability handshake).
+- Any change to the explorer contract, the CLI, the Rust core or the dev bridge:
+  `src/integrations/**`, `apps/desktop/src-tauri/**`, `apps/desktop/dev/**`,
+  `apps/desktop/src/platform/metaproject.ts`. A parallel session is fixing the backend defects there
+  (unstable v2 snapshot id, per-request staleness check, exact-match capability handshake).
+- Per-request latency (about 0.8 s per read) and read cancellation or queueing.
+- A redesign of the OpenSpec view.
+- Actions on a found object beyond "Copy path" (open in Files, send to a session, start a flow).
+- New screenshots for `docs/docs/images/desktop-metaproject/` (they need a native capture).
+- New dependencies: the graph stays on core `cytoscape`.

+# Implementation Plan
+
+Status: formalized (orchestrator, 2026-11-23)
+
+## Approach
+
+Frontend-only change inside `apps/desktop/src/metaproject/` plus one mount change in
+`apps/desktop/src/App.tsx`. The explorer contract, the CLI, the Rust core and the dev bridge stay
+as they are; the graph stays on core `cytoscape` (no new dependency).
+
+The work is cut so that three implementers can run at once on disjoint files, followed by one
+integration task:
+
+1. **Wave 1, in parallel** — T5 and T6 only add new files; T7 edits existing ones. Nothing in
+   wave 1 changes a file another wave-1 task owns, and the tree type-checks after each of them.
+2. **Wave 2** — T8 swaps the new graph and panel into the explorer, removes the code they replace,
+   and tidies the layout.
+3. **Then** — T9 (guide), T10 (full checks), T11 (live browser verification by the orchestrator),
+   T4 (review round).
+
+Rejected alternatives:
+
+- *One implementer, one task.* Smallest coordination cost, but a 920-line file rewritten in one
+  dispatch has no verification point until the end.
+- *`cose` / `breadthfirst` / `concentric` layouts of core cytoscape.* None can put incoming
+  neighbours on one side and outgoing on the other; `concentric` is today's ring with a second
+  radius. A computed `preset` layout is deterministic and unit-testable.
+- *`cytoscape-dagre`.* Would layer depth-2 paths with crossing minimisation, but adds a dependency
+  for a depth of at most two.
+- *Lifting explorer state into a store to survive unmount.* More code than keeping the view mounted
+  after its first visit, which is how the session view already behaves.
+
+## Design direction
+
+There is no `DESIGN.md` in the repository. This section is the direction for this flow; it is
+derived from the app's existing tokens and screens and introduces no new visual language.
+
+- **Tokens only.** Colours, spacing, type sizes and radii come from
+  `apps/desktop/src/styles/tokens.css` and work in every palette of `themes.css`. No raw colour
+  values in components or CSS; cytoscape gets its colours by resolving tokens at runtime.
+- **Type.** Three sizes in the panel: `--fs-lg` (title), `--fs-md` (body, rows), `--fs-sm` (meta,
+  section headings). Section headings are `--fs-sm`, weight 650, `--fg-muted`. Paths are monospace.
+- **One primary action per surface.** Other actions are quiet (`.btn-ghost` or icon buttons).
+- **Meaning is never colour alone.** Node kinds differ by shape or border style and are named in a
+  legend; relationship kinds are named in group captions and differ by line style.
+- **Reuse.** `.info-panel` / `.info-section` / `.info-row`, `.badge`, `.chip-btn`, `.tabs` / `.tab`
+  with `.tab-count`, `.section-title`, `.activity-row`, `EmptyState`, `Spinner`, `.side-resize`,
+  `Icon`. A new class is added only where none of these fits, and lives in the task's own CSS file.
+- **States.** Every data area has loading, empty (specific reason and an action), error (cause and
+  Retry) and limited (says what is hidden) states. Focus rings stay visible; targets are at least
+  24×24 px; motion respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.
+
+### Graph: a local neighbourhood in columns
+
+Layout is computed by a pure function and handed to cytoscape as `preset` positions.
+
+- Columns, left to right: second-step incoming · incoming · **root** · outgoing · second-step
+  outgoing. A neighbour whose only edges with the root point at the root is *incoming*; one the root
+  points at is *outgoing*; one with both is placed with outgoing. A second-step node goes to the
+  outer column on the side of the first-step node it is attached to.
+- Inside a column nodes are grouped by relationship kind (in the order of
+  `METAPROJECT_EDGE_KINDS_V2`), then sorted by title. Each group has a caption such as
+  "imports · 15".
+- A column shows at most 12 nodes; the rest collapse into one "+N more" entry at the bottom of the
+  column. Hidden neighbours stay reachable in the panel's relationship list.
+- Nodes are rounded rectangles with the label inside, 24 px high, width from the label, at most
+  about 132 px (root up to 180 px); long labels are shortened in the middle so a file extension
+  survives. Column gap about 44 px, row pitch about 30 px. These numbers may be tuned as long as the
+  acceptance criteria hold.
+- Node kind → shape and tint: module (thicker `--fg-muted` border), file (plain), symbol (barrel),
+  wiki (cut rectangle, `--info`), spec and change (tag shape, `--ok` / `--warn`), archive (tag shape,
+  dashed border). The root keeps its kind's shape with an `--accent` border and `--bg-selected` fill.
+- Relationship kind → line style: solid for `imports`, `calls`, `asset`; dashed for `describes`,
+  `links`, `changes-spec`, `spec-context`; dotted for `contains`, `defines`. Module imports with a
+  `count` are thicker. Second-step edges are fainter.
+- Zoom: fit, but never automatically below 0.8 (12 px labels stay ≥ 9.6 px) or above 1.15. When the
+  layout is wider than the box at 0.8, centre on the root and let the user pan. Wheel zoom and three
+  overlay buttons (zoom in, zoom out, fit) are available; nodes are not draggable.
+- Overlay (HTML, not canvas): a caption "<root title> · N incoming · M outgoing" (plus "limited"
+  when the projection is truncated) and a legend listing only the node kinds and line styles present.
+- Interaction: tap a node selects it; tap "+N more" asks the host to reveal the relationship list;
+  hover highlights a node with its edges and fades the rest.
+- Lifecycle: one cytoscape instance per mount; a new projection replaces elements in a batch; the
+  select callback is read through a ref; colours are re-resolved when `data-theme` or
+  `data-palette` changes on the document element; label size follows `--text-scale`.
+- The canvas stays `aria-hidden`; the keyboard and screen-reader path is the relationship list.
+
+### Panel: a summary of the node
+
+- Header: kind badge with icon, close button; title; path in monospace with a "Copy path" control.
+- Facts (`.info-row`): module (files), page type and status (wiki, as a badge), line (symbols),
+  relationship counts "N incoming · M outgoing" from the current projection, with "limited" when it
+  is truncated.
+- One tab bar with counts: **Relationships** · **Wiki** · **OpenSpec**. Relationships is the default.
+- Relationships: adjacent relationships grouped by direction, then by kind; a row is the other
+  node's title, a kind badge and its path, and selects that node. Second-step relationships are a
+  separate group where each row names both ends and can open either. Evidence is shown as at most
+  two example lines; digests are not shown.
+- Wiki / OpenSpec: today's behaviour (linked documents, suggested component page, preview, Open,
+  Find, Draft), with a preview cleaned of Markdown markers and of the "Covers:" metadata line.
+- Docked on wide hosts with a resize handle; on a host narrower than 820 px it is a right-anchored
+  drawer that leaves part of the content visible, takes focus on open and returns it on close.
+  Docked, it does not move focus when it opens.
+

+## Interfaces between tasks
+
+T8 integrates against exactly these exports. T5 and T6 may add optional props; they may not rename
+or drop these.
+
+```tsx
+// apps/desktop/src/metaproject/RelationshipGraph.tsx  (T5)
+export function RelationshipGraph(props: {
+  projection: MetaprojectNeighbors;                 // root = the selected node
+  busy?: boolean;                                    // a newer projection is loading: keep rendering, mark aria-busy, dim
+  onSelect: (id: string) => void;                    // a node was tapped
+  onShowHidden?: (side: "incoming" | "outgoing") => void; // a "+N more" entry was tapped

+
+// apps/desktop/src/metaproject/RelationshipList.tsx  (T6) — same name and props as today's export in MetaprojectView.tsx
+export function RelationshipList(props: {
+  projection: MetaprojectNeighbors;
+  select: (id: string) => void;

+
+// apps/desktop/src/metaproject/NodeDetailsPanel.tsx  (T6)
+export const isOpenSpecNode: (node: MetaprojectNode) => boolean;
+export function NodeDetailsPanel(props: {
+  node: MetaprojectNode;
+  relationships: MetaprojectNeighbors | null;        // filtered neighbourhood of `node`; null while loading or after a failure
+  relationshipsPending: boolean;
+  relationshipsProblem: string;                      // "" when none
+  revealRelationships?: number;                      // when this number changes: show the Relationships tab and scroll it into view
+  documents: MetaprojectNeighbors | null;            // linked-document neighbourhood (today's `projection` prop)
+  documentsPending: boolean;                         // today's `pending`

+  width?: number;
+  onResize: (width: number) => void;
+  onClose: () => void;
+  onSelect: (id: string) => void;                    // select a neighbour in the graph

+## State × event matrix
+
+Rows are states the explorer can be in; columns are the events this change reaches. A cell says
+what the user sees and which state survives. "—" means the event cannot happen in that state;
+"no change" means today's behaviour is kept.
+
+| state \ event | select a node (list, graph, panel row) | change a Graph filter | switch view (Graph / Wiki / OpenSpec) | leave the work view and return | Back | Retry / Refresh | theme or palette change | rebuild finishes |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| negotiating the protocol | — | — | no change | still negotiating; result applied on arrival (AC10) | — | — | no change | — |
+| negotiation failed | — | — | banner stays | banner and Retry still there (AC10) | — | re-negotiates; banner stays until success; no "Loading…" next to the error (AC15) | no change | — |
+| catalog loaded, nothing loading | new selection is a history entry (AC11); the list row is selected and scrolled into view (AC17) | relationships re-read with the new filters; not a history entry | each view keeps its own query and selection (no change) | mode, query, selection, filters, panel state and history are as they were (AC10) | previous selection, panel state and scroll restored (AC11) | no change | graph re-coloured in place, no selection change needed (AC6) | — |
+| relationships loading for a new selection | the newest selection wins; stale responses are dropped (no change) | same | Wiki's relationships use fixed defaults, never Graph's filters (AC13) | load continues, result applied on arrival (AC10) | previous route; stale response dropped | no change | no change | — |
+| … while a previous graph exists | previous graph stays rendered, marked busy, until the new one arrives (AC17) | same | — | — | same | — | — | — |
+| relationships failed | no change (error does not follow to the new selection) | re-read | no change | error still shown | no change | no change | — | — |
+| projection limited (truncated) | no change | no change | no change | no change | no change | no change | no change | — |
+| … column over the cap | "+N more" reveals the relationship list in the panel (AC2, AC8) | — | — | — | — | — | — | — |
+| snapshot mismatch | no change | no change | no change | banner still shown | no change | catalog re-read (no change) | — | — |
+| rebuilding the graph | allowed; rebuild continues | allowed | allowed | rebuild continues; button state correct on return | allowed | allowed; the rebuild's end still re-enables the button and re-reads the catalog (AC14) | — | button enabled again and catalog re-read, whatever reloaded meanwhile (AC14) |
+| Wiki with a query and no hits | — | no effect on Wiki (AC13) | no change | as left | previous route | — | — | — |
+| … arrived through "Find a Wiki page" | — | — | — | — | returns to the graph node | — | — | — |
+| … what the article area shows | an empty state naming the query, never an unrelated article (AC12) | | | | | | | |
+| typing in the search field | — | — | — | query kept | query edits are not history entries (AC11) | — | — | — |
+| Wiki article open, link clicked | target not loaded → one lookup read, then open; unresolved → inline message naming the path (AC16) | — | — | — | returns to the article | — | — | — |

+## Steps
+
+1. T5 — graph layout module and `RelationshipGraph` (new files).
+2. T6 — `NodeDetailsPanel` and `RelationshipList` (new files).
+3. T7 — navigation and state fixes D1–D7 in the explorer, the navigation hook and `App.tsx`.
+4. T8 — integrate T5 and T6 into the explorer; move the relationship list into the panel; compact,
+   labelled filters; counts in the list header; keep the previous graph while loading; delete the
+   replaced code and styles.
+5. T9 — update the Desktop Metaproject guide.
+6. T10 — desktop typecheck and the full desktop test suite.
+7. T11 — live browser verification (dev build) at 1180×780, 1440×900 and 720×480, dark and light.
+8. T4 — review round, fix rounds as needed.
+
+## Risks
+
+- **cytoscape under happy-dom.** The existing tests never mount the canvas. T5 keeps layout and
+  style mapping in pure, tested functions and keeps caption and legend in HTML; if cytoscape cannot
+  mount in happy-dom the component test injects a stand-in for the cytoscape factory and says so.
+- **Visual tuning without a browser.** Implementers verify with tests and the type checker; the
+  orchestrator verifies the render in T11. A fix round after T11 is expected and budgeted.
+- **Three lanes in one worktree.** Disjoint file ownership (table above), no `git stash`, no
+  `git add -A`, commits only by the orchestrator at task boundaries with explicit paths. A lane
+  that sees type errors in another lane's in-progress files reports them and does not touch them.
+- **`MetaprojectView.tsx` is edited by T7 and then T8.** They run one after the other.
+- **Parallel backend session** edits `apps/desktop/src/platform/metaproject.ts`; this flow does not.
+- **Keeping the view mounted** keeps its effects alive while hidden; the graph must tolerate a
+  zero-size container (it already guards `fit` on size).

# Explore project knowledge in Keryx Desktop
 
 Open **Metaproject** in a project window, or press **⌘5**. Use **Graph** to
 trace relationships between project objects and **Wiki** to read articles.
-Each view remembers its own search and selection. **Back** restores the
-previous view, including the search and scroll position. The explorer
-reads the open checkout locally and works without a GitHub account or a model
-provider.
+Each view remembers its own search and selection. **Back** steps back through
+the items you selected, not only through view switches, and restores the
+search and scroll position of each step. If you leave the Metaproject tab and
+return, the explorer keeps its view, search, selection and filters. The
+explorer reads the open checkout locally and works without a GitHub account or
+a model provider.
 
 ## Browse OpenSpec
 
 Select **OpenSpec** to browse **Specs**, **Changes** and **Archive** from the
 open checkout. Requirements and scenarios show their source; archived changes
 provide historical context. Select **Archive** to search historical changes.
 **Open current spec** opens the linked specification directly. Use **View in
 Graph** when you want to explore its relationships. Missing or partial
 OpenSpec data does not prevent using Graph and Wiki.
 
 The same checkout-local reader is available in a terminal or Keryx Shell:
 
 ```bash
 keryx openspec list --kind spec --json
 keryx openspec search "review" --scope all --json
 keryx openspec show openspec/specs/review/spec.md --json
 ```
 
 ## Set up the project
 
 1. Install [Keryx Desktop and its matching CLI](../desktop-app.md#install).
    In Desktop, use **Open Folder…** to open the repository or worktree you
    want to explore.
 2. If the repository already has a `.metaproject/`, use that workspace.
    Otherwise, initialize it from the repository root.
 
    ```bash
    keryx init --yes
    ```
 
-3. Open **Metaproject** and select **Rebuild graph** when the view reports
-   **Graph missing** or **Graph stale**. The terminal panel shows the build
-   progress. You can also build it from the same checkout in a terminal.
+3. Open **Metaproject** and select **Rebuild graph** when the banner reads
+   **Graph is missing.** or **Graph is stale.** The banner is one line. Select
+   **Details** beside it to read the reason. The terminal panel shows the
+   build progress. You can also build it from the same checkout in a terminal.
 
    ```bash
    keryx gdgraph build
    ```
 
 4. If the wiki is empty, create pages for the components and architecture the
    team wants to document. To start with graph-derived component drafts,
    run `keryx wiki collect --limit 10`. To write a page by hand, scaffold it
    with `keryx wiki new` and edit the resulting Markdown under
    `.metaproject/wiki/`.
 
    ```bash
    keryx wiki new architecture event-delivery --title "Event delivery"
    keryx wiki index
    keryx wiki validate
    ```
 
    Reopen **Metaproject** to see new pages. Rebuild the graph after changing
    which code a page covers so the `describes` relationships reflect the
    change. Review generated drafts before relying on their prose. See the
    [wiki module](../modules.md#gdwiki) for page types and lifecycle.
 
 ### Enable symbol and call relationships
 
 Files, modules, wiki pages and import relationships work with the file
-graph. For symbol search and the **defines** and **calls** filters, enable the
-optional symbol layer per checkout and rebuild it.

 ## Trace relationships in Graph
 
-![Graph view with Agent Bus selected, its related code highlighted, and the relationship controls and list visible](../images/desktop-metaproject/graph.jpg)
-
-1. Select a starting item. Use **Direction → Outgoing** to follow its
-   dependencies or links, and **Incoming** to see what points to it.
-   **Both** includes each direction.
-2. Start at **1 step** for direct neighbors. Use **2 steps** to follow those
-   neighbors one level further. Turn off unrelated relationship types to
-   narrow a busy graph.
-3. Click a node to select it and open the details pane. Use its **Wiki** or
-   **OpenSpec** tab to preview linked documents, then open the full document
-   with the named action. Drag the divider, or focus it and use the arrow
-   keys, to change the pane width. Press **Escape** to close it. You can also
-   select a neighboring node with **Tab** and **Enter** in the relationship list.
-   A relationship between two second-step items offers an **Open** button for
-   each endpoint.
-4. Read the relationship row for the exact path or source evidence when
-   available. Check the arrow direction before following a dependency.
-
-| Type | Direction |
-| --- | --- |
-| `imports` | A source file or module points to an imported file or module. |
-| `asset` | A source file points to an asset it references. |
-| `describes` | A wiki page points to code it covers. |
-| `links` | A wiki page points to another page in the wiki. |
-| `contains` | A module points to a file it contains. |
-| `defines` | A file or symbol points to a symbol it defines. |
-| `calls` | An indexed caller points to a resolved callee. |

+
+The graph shows a local neighborhood of the selected item in columns. What
+points at the selected item is on its left, and what it points at is on its
+right. In the picture, `src/bus/leases.ts` is selected: the files that import
+it, the Agent Bus page that describes it and its module are on the left, and
+the four files it imports are on the right. With **2 steps**, items one step
+further out sit in additional columns beyond those, drawn fainter. The
+header row above the graph shows its caption, the zoom controls and the
+**Filters** button.
+
+1. Select a starting item, such as `src/bus/leases.ts`. The graph shows
+   what points to it and what it points at. Use **Filters** to follow only one
+   direction.
+2. Select **Filters** in the header row of the graph, next to the zoom
+   controls. A popover opens with the graph visible behind it, and every change
+   applies at once. Press **Escape** or click outside to close it.
+   - **Direction**: **Outgoing** follows dependencies or links, **Incoming**
+     shows what points to the item, and **Both** includes each direction.
+   - **Depth**: start at **1 step** for direct neighbors. Use **2 steps** to
+     follow those neighbors one level further.
+   - **Relationship types**: turn off unrelated types to narrow a busy graph.
+     They are named **Imports**, **Assets**, **Describes**, **Wiki links**,
+     **Contains**, **Defines**, **Calls**, **Changes spec** and **Spec
+     context**. **Defines** and **Calls** are disabled, with the reason
+     shown, until the symbol layer is enabled.
+   - **Reset filters** restores the defaults. While the filters differ from
+     their defaults, the button reads **Filters · n** and is highlighted.
+3. Read the groups. Each group of items has a caption with its relationship
+   type and a count, for example **Imports · 7**. A column shows at most 12
+   items. When a column has more, it keeps a few items from each
+   relationship type and collapses the rest into a **+N more** entry. Click it
+   to open the full list in the **Relationships** tab of the details panel.
+4. Use the legend under the graph to read the shapes and lines. The shape and
+   border of an item show its kind, such as module, file, symbol, Wiki page,
+   spec or change. The line style shows the relationship family: solid,
+   dashed or dotted, with the relationship types that use it. The legend lists
+   only what the current graph contains. Meaning never depends on color alone.
+5. Use the zoom in, zoom out and fit controls in the graph's header row to
+   move around a large neighborhood. Click an item to select it. The graph re-centers on it,
+   and while its relationships load the previous graph stays on screen,
+   dimmed. **Back** returns to the item you selected before.
+6. Read the details panel for the selected item. It shows the kind, the title
+   and the path, with a **Copy path** control. Below are the facts: the
+   module, the page type, the status and the relationship counts. Drag the
+   divider, or focus it and use the arrow keys, to change the panel width.
+   Press **Escape** to close it. Three tabs, each with a count, follow the
+   facts:
+
+   - **Relationships** is the default tab. It groups the relationships into
+     **Incoming** and **Outgoing**, then by type. Click a row to select that
+     item, or focus it with **Tab** and press **Enter**. The control at the end
+     of a row opens the source evidence for that relationship, when there is
+     any. For module imports it reads the count, such as **7 imports**;
+     otherwise it reads **N examples**. Relationships between two second-step
+     items sit in a **Second step** disclosure, closed until you open it. Each
+     relationship offers an **Open** button for each endpoint. Check the direction before
+     following a dependency.
+   - **Wiki** previews the linked Wiki page. **Open in Wiki** opens the full
+     page. When no page is linked, **Find a Wiki page** searches for one and
+     **Draft Wiki page** starts a session that prepares a draft.
+   - **OpenSpec** works the same way for specs and changes, with **Open in
+     OpenSpec**, **Find an OpenSpec document** and **Draft OpenSpec change**.

 ## Data, checkout boundaries and limits
 
 | Layer | Source | How it changes |
 | --- | --- | --- |
 | Wiki | Markdown under `.metaproject/wiki/` | Edit the project pages or use the wiki CLI. |
 | File and symbol graph | Generated gdgraph artifacts for the open checkout | Run **Rebuild graph** or `keryx gdgraph build`. |
 | Selection and filters | The active Desktop view | Search, select a result, or change the view controls. |
 
 Desktop sends read requests for catalog, search, detail, and neighbors through
 the local Keryx CLI. It reads from the project folder associated with the
 view. A Git worktree has its own graph freshness and may show a different
 catalog from the main checkout. Desktop checks graph freshness when it loads
 the catalog; search, detail and neighbor reads skip that check. Read requests
 leave your files alone. **Rebuild graph** writes the generated graph artifacts.
